text: [word/document.xml] 1 3175 Supplementary Figure 1. Representative pictures of the agar diffusion assay used to evaluate the antimicrobial activity of peptide fractions (PFs) isolated from the hemolymph of H. illucens larvae. The assay was performed against various human pathogenic bacterial strains, including Escherichia coli enteroinvasive (EIEC), Staphylococcus aureus , Pseudomonas aeruginosa , Salmonella Typhimurium, Streptococcus pyogenes , Enterococcus faecalis , and Proteus mirabilis . Wells contain PFs obtained from ( a ) uninfected larvae (CTRL), ( b ) larvae infected with Escherichia coli , and ( c ) larvae infected with Micrococcus flavus . Each image is representative of three independent biological replicates. Supplementary Figure 2. Representative pictures of the agar diffusion assay used to assess the antimicrobial activity of peptide fractions (PFs) isolated from the hemolymph of H. illucens larvae against antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains, including carbapenem-resistant Klebsiella pneumoniae (CRKP 70131, 70461, 742, 5) and methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus aureus (MRSA), as well as the fungal strain Candida albicans . Wells contain PFs from ( a ) uninfected larvae (CTRL ), ( b ) larvae infected with Escherichia coli and ( c ) larvae infected with Micrococcus flavus . Each image is representative of three independent biological replicates.

Colony-forming unit (CFU/mL) counts obtained from minimum bactericidal concentration (MBC) assays performed on pathogenic and antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains, as well as the opportunistic fungus Candida albicans , treated with peptide fractions (PFs) isolated from the hemolymph of H. illucens larvae. PFs were obtained from uninfected larvae (CTRL), larvae infected with Escherichia coli and larvae infected with Micrococcus flavus . Tested concentrations ranged from 0.023 to 0.750 µg·µL⁻¹ . The MBC was defined as the lowest concentration at which no bacterial or fungal growth (CFU = 0) was detected. Data are expressed as CFUs/mL and represent the mean values of three independent biological replicates.
